messages.text:
I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sorry your miner arrived with a problem, let's figure out what's going on.

Is this the Hammer Thor P2 from order Shop····? And what exactly happens when you plug it in? For example:

1. It doesn't power on at all (no lights, no fans)
2. It powers on but shows an error on the screen
3. It runs, but the hashrate is low or zero
4. Something is physically damaged (screen, fan, case)

If there's an error on the screen, a photo of it would help a lot.

Hello!

I'm writing to follow up on my Thor P2. I believe it is damaged, I'm not sure maybe there could possibly be some other issue I'm not seeing. Immediately after unboxing it on the first power up I got a red "power board error." This is always followed up very quickly by a red "over temp" error that will make it restart, where it over temps again 10-20 seconds after restart. The room it's in is about 72 degrees farenheit and the miner is in a well ventilated spot. At a glance, I don't see any parts that immediately look weird or broken from a quick look.

Let me know what you think,

JonPaul R.
Let me check what that "power board error" means on the Thor P2 first.
Searched the web · Hammer Thor P2 "power board error" over temp
Searched the web · Hammer Thor P2 miner error codes troubleshooting
Searched the web · harlolabs Harlo OS Thor P2 firmware

Thanks for the detail, JonPaul. Getting a power board error and then over temp within seconds of the first boot, in a 72°F room, isn't normal. I couldn't find any official Hammer or Harlo documentation for that exact "power board error" on the Thor P2, so I won't guess what it means. Let's narrow it down.

For now, **keep it unplugged** between tests so it doesn't keep cycling hot.

Next, please do one test boot and tell me:

1. **Fans:** in those 10 to 20 seconds before the over temp, are the fans spinning? Do they spin up fast, slow, or not at all?
2. **Power supply:** are you using the power supply that came in the box? Is it plugged straight into a wall outlet, or through a power strip or extension cord?
3. **Firmware:** if the screen or web UI shows a firmware version before it restarts, what is it?

If you can, also send a **short video** of one boot from power-on through the over temp restart, and a **clear photo of the serial number** label. Those settle it much faster than a description.

Once I have that, I'll know whether this is a power supply problem or something on the board itself.
Fans spin at a normal speed, pretty fast. I am using the power supply from the box straight into a wall outlet. When it was on last I check and it said firmware was up to date

Thanks. That rules out a few things: the fans work, and you're on the stock power supply plugged straight into the wall. So it's not a cooling or airflow problem.

Fans running fast plus an over temp within seconds usually means one of two things. Either the miner is reading a wrong temperature, or one spot on the board really is heating up very fast. The temperature readings will tell us which.

On the next test boot, please note:

1. **Temperatures:** what temperature numbers show on the screen or in the web UI (browse to the miner's IP) just before the over temp? Note every reading if there is more than one, and whether it climbs gradually or jumps straight to a high number.
2. **Firmware number:** the version number itself (for example "v1.x.x"), not just "up to date".

A **short video** of one boot from power-on to the restart would cap····, along with the **photo of the serial number** label.

Unplug it after that test. If anything smells hot or burnt, unplug it right away and don't power it on again.
